Didn’t expect to find myself in a University of Cincinnati article, but here we are 🚀 A year ago, right after Origin Ventures Office of Entrepreneurship iVenture 11 summer session, two friends and I booked one-way flights to San Francisco with zero connections and barely a plan. We ended up living out of a sketchy basement Airbnb, surviving on caffeine, toast, and the belief that if we put ourselves in the right rooms long enough, something would happen. In 21 days, that trip somehow turned into this: • Won the world’s largest smart glasses hackathon at Y Combinator • Had investors offer us $500k to keep building • Connected with founders who offered us internships on the spot • Made friends with some of the smartest, most ambitious people from around the world Most opportunities in life are on the other side of simply deciding to take the leap and show up. If you’re a builder working on a startup, or someone who wants to work at one, take the trip to SF, it’ll pay for itself. https://lnkd.in/g5WNTviG Shoutout Pratyush Srivastava and Aleksandar Ilijevski for agreeing to share a cold, dingy basement studio with absolutely no guarantee any of this would work out 🙌 ...more

OpenAI 's ChatGPT just turned 3 years old, and what have we learned? A LOT. 😅 We traced the full arc, from the first jailbreaks and prompt injection experiments in late 2022, through the plugin era and its third-party risks, to the memory feature that let attackers plant instructions persisting across sessions, and finally to today's autonomous agents browsing the web and taking actions on your behalf. Three years in, the security community knows what it's up against, but these aren't easy problems to solve. Get the breakdown in our latest blog: https://lnkd.in/dn4jqC98 #chatgpt #aisecurity #cybersecurity ...more ...more

HUGE update- Everyone’s talking about AI, but almost no one’s ready for what it’s breaking in security. We just launched the 2025 State of AI Security Report, surveying 275 security and IT leaders across industries, and the results show just how fast enterprise security is being rewritten: • 70% don’t have optimized AI governance • Half expect data breaches through AI tools this year • CIOs now lead AI security — CISOs rank fourth • AI supply chain security tops the 2025 budget list • Runtime is both the #1 vulnerability and the least prepared phase Traditional “shift-left” approaches don’t fit this new reality anymore. Proud to be a part of the amazing team at Acuvity , where we’re building security for the AI era. Full report: https://lnkd.in/ge2Du-9y Press coverage: https://lnkd.in/gjcw_MHw ...more

A lot can change in a year. This time a year ago, I was wrapping up my internship at Handshake, excited to be coming back full time as an iOS engineer. Two months later, I became one of the founding members of the FDE team, a team that has since grown to over 20 engineers and has gone international. I distinctly remember asking Matt Greenberg when given the offer to join: “So like, what does an FDE even do” Which I still think is a totally valid question. I’ve spoken with many other FDEs around the bay and it looks different at every company. FDE at Handshake is the perfect firehose of technical and operational complexity combined with the benefit of building 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘫𝘶𝘴𝘵 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩, but 𝘰𝘯 the frontier of AI. It feels like the exact kind of role that gives you 3 years of engineering experience in 1. The last 10 months building this team has been incredible, and I’m grateful to have had such tremendous growth this year. I have an unlimited amount of people to thank, but shoutout to Shaashwat Sharma and Avery Yip who supported my development during the early days, Jon Rahoi for convincing me to dive 10 toes deep when I was unsure about the transition, Alden Roberts for the trust and guidance in getting our team to the next level, and most importantly to Calum Crawford for being my perfect half in building this team together. Truly would not be possible without these folks. A lot can happen in a year, and we’ve barely cracked the surface. Let’s keep building!

OpenVector (YC S26) is an AI that turns any camera into an autonomous worker. Every important business moment happens in the physical world — someone tailgates, a production cycle stalls, a worker skips a safety step, or a customer arrives. And every camera on the planet only records it for later. For physical operations, the best technology available was a human staring at a monitor. So Andrey Gizdov (PhD dropout at Harvard) and Vishal Urlam (CMU engineer) built OpenVector. No new hardware or expensive setups, just an app. You simply describe your task in plain English, and OpenVector auto-builds a custom AI model for it and watches your feeds 24/7 in real-time. OpenVector also does something no standard camera system can: it operates a computer just like a human based on what it sees. It automatically integrates with legacy systems to make a call, send an email, update your POS or CRM, or trigger a webhook the second an event happens. OpenVector is already live and seeing use cases tracking production cycles, ensuring good manufacturing practices, and catching physical design errors across security, retail, and logistics. There are over 1 billion cameras worldwide, and almost all of them stop at seeing. Until today. OpenVector enables any camera to do real work. Congrats on the launch, Andrey and Vishal! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/g4Yy_SMb
